topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines how the session will integrate previously learned immune mechanisms to explain the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate recognition of pathogens and cellular damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sentinel cells and pattern recognition receptors detect microbial components and cellular damage to initiate an innate immune response.

topics.label: Leukocyte recruitment and systemic inflammatory consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how immune cells migrate into inflamed tissues and lymphatic vessels, as well as the physiological hazards of uncontrolled systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Inflammation resolution, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory states
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms responsible for shutting down acute inflammation, restoring damaged tissue, and establishing chronic inflammatory or granulomatous responses when resolution fails.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and previews the subject of the upcoming class.
